GovernmentDefenseTelecom OperatorsDirectory

A country-by-country briefing on the leading mobile network operators and defense contractors in the 36 EU and NATO member countries, with space and satcom companies highlighted. Telecom market shares come from national regulators where available, and defense rankings from the Defense News Top 100 and SIPRI Top 100.

Top Telecommunications Operators and Defense Contractors

in EU and NATO Member Countries

36 countries | 27 EU member states + 32 NATO allies | incl. space & satcom companies

Research briefing - as of 26 October 2026

Every figure is linked to the source it was taken from (see each table and the consolidated Sources section).

1. Introduction, methodology and caveats

This briefing lists, for each of the 36 countries that belong to the European Union and/or NATO, the leading telecommunications operators and the leading defense contractors, with space and satellite-communications (satcom) companies highlighted where they are significant for government and military users. Countries are presented alphabetically, each with a telecom table and a defense table.

Scope

  • Countries: 27 EU member states and 32 NATO members = 36 countries (23 belong to both; Austria, Cyprus, Ireland and Malta are EU-only; the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Norway, Iceland, Turkiye, Albania, Montenegro and North Macedonia are NATO-only).
  • Telecom: typically the 2-4 largest mobile network operators, ranked by the regulator's (or best available) subscriber share.
  • Defense: typically 2-5 companies; up to ~8-12 for the United States and the largest European producers. Where a country has no notable defense industry, this is stated.
  • Space & satcom: satellite operators, manufacturers and launch companies relevant to government/military satcom (e.g. SES, Eutelsat/OneWeb, Hispasat, Hisdesat, Telesat, Viasat/Inmarsat, Iridium, SpaceX, Amazon Leo, Space Norway, Telespazio, Avio, OHB, ICEYE).

Methodology and sources

  • Telecom market share: national telecom regulators were used first (e.g. RTR, BIPT, CRC, HAKOM, CTU, TTJA, Traficom, BNetzA, EETT, NMHH, Fjarskiptastofa, ComReg, AGCOM, ILR, EKIP, ACM, Nkom, UKE, ANACOM, ANCOM, AKOS, CNMC, PTS, BTK). Where a regulator does not publish operator-level shares (France, UK, US, Canada) operator-reported subscriber bases or industry-association compilations are shown instead.
  • Defense size: the Defense News Top 100 (2026 list, fiscal-2025 defense revenue, US$) and the SIPRI Top 100 Arms-producing and Military Services Companies, 2024 (published December 2025, arms revenue in constant 2024 US$; this is the latest SIPRI edition as of October 2026). Both ranks are shown when available. For companies outside both rankings, revenue from company annual reports, official registries or reputable press is given; if no reliable figure was found the entry says 'Not publicly reported'.
  • Verification: every number in this document comes from a source opened during research on 26 Oct 2026; each table row links to its source(s) by number, and all sources are listed with hyperlinks and years in the final Sources section. Company website links are official home pages.

Caveats

  • Data years vary: telecom figures range from 2024 to Q2 2026 depending on what each regulator has published; defense revenues are FY2025 (Defense News) or calendar 2024 (SIPRI).
  • Market-share definitions differ: some regulators count active SIMs excluding M2M/IoT (Austria, Portugal, Turkiye), others registered SIM profiles including M2M (Germany - which inflates Vodafone's share), subscribers of voice service (Bulgaria), total market revenue (Lithuania), or publish only ranges (Belgium, Netherlands). Shares are therefore not comparable across countries.
  • Defense metrics differ: SIPRI 'arms revenue' and Defense News 'defense revenue' use different definitions, currencies/price bases and fiscal years, so the two figures for one company differ. Multinationals are listed once, under their headquarters country, with cross-references for national subsidiaries (e.g. KNDS, MBDA, BAE Systems' Swedish units).
  • Secondary data: figures from secondary press or registries are labelled as such; estimates are labelled 'estimated'. Figures computed by us (e.g. shares from subscriber counts) are labelled 'computed'.

Legend

  • Sector: Telecom - network operator; Defense - defense contractor; Space & satcom - satellite operator/manufacturer/launch; Dual - significant in both telecom and defense.
  • Membership: 'EU', 'NATO' or 'EU + NATO' membership as of 26 Oct 2026.
